## TL;DR

The client project board presents existing project tasks in three read-only columns. This session repaired the route registrations that caused the previous handoff validation to fail.

## Work and rationale

The board groups inbox and ready tasks as Planned, active tasks as Building, and review tasks as Reviewed, omitting done tasks. It displays the project name, a short description, and each task's identifier, title and state-derived status. The Work page links to the view; it does not expose task-operation controls on that view. The marketing illustration remains unchanged.

The previous validation identified two registries that had not been updated for the new route. Added `/client-board` to the app screenshot route prefixes so declared shots resolve to the app target, and to the loading skeleton routes so it has an explicit loading presentation. Reused the existing three-column board skeleton and added a matching loading header. Tests cover these behaviors and the existing registry consistency checks guard the broader class of missing route registrations.

## Approaches tried

Reused existing task data, status mapping and skeleton components rather than introducing a separate task model or a new loading component. Declared a review shot of the board through RepoOS.

## Challenges and blockers

The prior handoff failed in remote validation because the route was missing from both registrations. No review report was present in the worktree's review directory. Screenshot capture is owned by the handoff process, so its resulting image was not available for inspection during this session.

## Key learnings

Adding a UI route also requires registering it with screenshot target resolution and the app loading skeleton. The consistency tests make those dependencies visible when a new route is introduced.
